cards.typed_words:
Dear Kristin,
It is the tendency for a painter to paint with vivid colors. Just as it is natural for the accountant to deal with numbers. And poets, you might ask?...well they deal with imagery and symbolism. On the topic of imagery, well that is me and that is my life. I see life as a series of images and meanings represented through this imagery. It is my nature to see a certain side of someone or something and attempt to capture that emotion or feeling. I am realizing that you have represented beauty in my life. You were a symbol of purity and kindness. You provided me with a beacon of hope to which I could look to for support through the many dark tunnels that I have found myself lurking in. You have a set role in my life, a role from which you could never deviate from. You are support and a helping hand. In times of trouble and uneasiness you are there to comfort me. It is natural for me to make you into something that you are not or see you only as an ideal or an idol but reality must over take my poetic nature at sometime or another. This is a good time.
I used you to help myself and I realize that there is only a certain level that you can take me to. The rest I must go myself. Well you have taken me far and have led me to the gates of heaven. Now I must find my own way to sneak in. Perhaps when God is sleeping I can hop the fence?
I still have a little trouble with religious imagery. I am my own god and I do not follow his plan I make my own. If my actions are right and correct then I shall make myself a good life, if I screw up then I have no one to blame but myself. i live a life of no excuses anymore. I will not allow myself to wait forever for a plan that may or may not be guided by a hand above. I look for god in people and then follow them to a heaven on  [...cut for the check]

cards.typed_words: Hello, I'm sorry I haven't had the courage to talk to you since now but now is better than not at all. I do miss you and I do care about you and i still find myself thinking of you (how could i not) but I've been kind of afraid about where our relationship could go from this point. I am happy right now and I don't want that to change. I'm still afraid of looking into you big brown eyes and rekindling an old flame that could set the whole world on fire. I've been married to my school, poetry and family and friends but you're still grouped into each one of those categories so i know that i can never give you a goodbye forever type of note. I really, really wish that things would have worked out better between us because you are a very special girl with a lot of love and care inside you and sometimes i kick myself for letting you go (again) but I really think that the end was upon us. I had my ideals of love and I'm not too sure that any one could measure up to such a high expectation. Towards the end I found myself thinking that I was short changing you because I wondered who you wouldn't meet or date because I was in the picture. I realized that your real true love could be standing right next to you and you might let him (or her:) walk right past forever. I couldn't bare it anymore. cards.summary: A printed piece of paper.
cards.typed_words:
Hello,
I called you but you weren't home. As I stood waitingly listening to the receiver, my heart beat with the same rhythm as the ringing of the unanswered phone. With each new ring I began to feel my happiness fade for it meant that each ring brought me father away from the sweet sunshine of your voice. The initial excitement that swept through me like a summer breeze through an open window dulled to a stagnance of a coffin, dark and void of hope. I reassured myself that you were just getting out of your car when I called or perhaps out of earshot when the phone last rang. Clinging to my hopes, like a child dreams of pokemon on Christmas morning, i called again. Again, as I heard each successive ring I pretended that you were walking in the door at that very moment. We are so close that I knew that you could feel me thinking of you. I imagined your footsteps running feverishly towards the phone in eager anticipation of the loved one who awaited. I held on and held on until the sound of the monotonous, busy ringing next to my ear saddened me to the harsh reality that you were not home. I collected myself and attempted to put forth a happy nature even though my insides were churning and my heart felt like an empty vessel, from which the blood that let it live had been painfully drained. My soul had escaped during the saddening rings of the call and was now searching for the love it once had known. It was searching for its place, its hope and its inspiration...My soul was searching for you. I set out to find my soul myself but I know deep down inside that I will only find it when I find you.

cards.name_on_card: There is only one person on this Earth who I have ever had
cards.summary: A piece of lined notebook paper featuring handwriting in dark ink.
cards.typed_words:
There is only one person on this Earth who I have ever had the courage to truly revealed myself to...
to everyone else I'm just a voice on a video, Telephone, a picture on a business card, a paragraph
in an email or a page in a book.
That's been my choice and has led to a
hollow existence... a collection of bits and
pieces that could never accurately portray what
is embodied in the whole... I'm trying to
change that. If I can then I think that
I shall find the fulfillment that my
heart is now seeking... if I can't then
let my failures act as a warning to
anyone who happens to read this... if I
do succeed, then look towards me for hope and
inspiration so that you might follow my
lead with your own carving
footsteps... within the mold of your
own contours and footprints.

Yet Regardless of where my fate lies on
whatever path I end up
on this great journey that is life just
know that there is wisdom to be found
in my story... in ALL of OUR
stories.
Much love,
Tom

cards.name_on_card: Will Elway retire? Try asking Jordan
cards.summary: Typed document paper sheets accompanied by handwritten number cards placed along the left side.
cards.typed_words:
My name is John Elway. I have just been named the MVP of the Superbowl and I may retire. I played minor league baseball (single A with the Yankees) and was MVP of the League in 1987. Did I mention I've been in 5 Superbowls?
Enter Mr. Jordan.
My name is Michael Jordan. I have just won the NBA Finals and was named the Final's MVP and I retired. I also played minor league baseball (double A with the WhiteSox) and was also MVP of the league in 1987. Did I mention I've been to the Finals 6 times and won all 6?
I give you this statement: No quarterback has ever won three Superbowls in a row. John Elway has won two in a row. I give you this question: Will Elway go out on top? I don't mean just any top we're talking tip of the iceberg here. He Has the best running back in football in Terrell Davis, one of the top tight ends in the game in Shannon Sharpe (although you wouldn't know it from watching the Big Game), and a defense good enough to hold Atlanta's offense to just 19 points.

Michael aside, Elway is still a top NFL quarterback who can lead his team to a win. Want further proof? How about more fourth quarter or overtime winning drives (47) than any other quarterback who ever lived. This year he threw for 22 touchdowns and only 10 interceptions, yes better then Drew "pull my finger" Bledsoe. He threw for 336 yards, including an 80 yard bomb to wide receiver Rod Smith, in the Superbowl after a poor performance in last year's win.
I think he will call it a career now that the season is over. He's played sixteen years, won the last two titles and can still walk. John has four kids and a lovely wife that would love to see him for more than six months a year. If he does end it I'm sure he could be the mayor of Denver (until Terrell retires with 12 consecutive MVP's).
Jessie 'Th [...cut for the check]

Here is the premise of my argument against the retiring of Tony
Conigliaro's number: The Red Sox have only retired five numbers in their ninety-
plus year history and the numbers that Tony C. put up while he was healthy are
not as good as comparable Red Sox Hall of Fame and number retiree hopefuls
Jim Rice and Dwight Evans. In a nutshell, Tony C. was a baseball player with an
incredibly high ceiling who was tragically beaned in the prime of his career,
resulting in his career being shortened and ultimately finished. Cincinnati Reds
first baseman Tony Perez has been inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame and
had his jersey retired by the Reds. Take a look at the statistics and pretend
you're the general manager of a team looking to make a big trade. If you could
trade for just one of these four players which one would you want? What if you
could retire just one of their numbers, who deserves it the most?
Jim Rice played in Boston for 16 years and Dwight Evans for 18. Tony C.
was here for just over six seasons. Will I be angered if the Red Sox retire Tony's
number? No, not at all. I would actually back the retiring of his number if the Sox
had about five of the following names/numbers up there right now: Cy Young,
Babe Ruth, El Tiante, Wade Boggs, Jimmie Foxx, Lee Smith, Jim Rice, Fred
Lynn, Dwight Evans, Duffy Lewis, Waite Hoyt, Johnny Pesky, Luis Aparicio, Tom
Seaver and of course, Lovable Lou Merloni.

Hearing on retired teachers' health insurance proposal Monday night

by Robert Curtin

LYNNFIELD  -  The Board of Selectmen will take up the issue of whether to switch retired teachers' health insurance from the state Group Insurance Commission to the town plan on Monday, August 11.

The selectmen will meet at 7:30 p.m. at the Lynnfield High School media center.

The committee to proceed the meeting was proposed by selectman William Gustus at the July 23 meeting.

Gustus said that while the town and state plans differ in some respects, the town plan is generally equivalent to and in some respects better than that plan retired teachers now have. He urged retired teachers to review the plans to best suited their particular needs. That to end, Gustus mailed a detailed report on the provisions of the state and town plans to all retired teachers.

Chairman of the Board of Selectmen Robert Whalen said it is the board's intention to vote on the matter after the hearing but during the same meeting.

The hearing will also include a vote of the retired teachers present; although state law requires that vote, it is not binding of the Board of Selectmen.

To make the change from the state to the town system, the Board of Selectmen would have to rescind the 1972 acceptance of a local option of state law.
